q: Which of these is one of the eight ramen preparations on the House of Umami wall chart?
choices: Tokyo Shoyu Ramen
Dragon Ramen
Mango Miso Ramen
Volcano Udon
why: Tokyo Shoyu Ramen is explicitly listed on the employee ramen reference. Learn the actual preparation from the chart rather than guessing from the name.

q: A guest asks what goes into a ramen they are considering. What is your best source for the documented preparation?
choices: Your memory of a similar dish elsewhere
The House of Umami ramen preparation and toppings chart
A guess based on the dish's name
A third-party delivery description
why: Use the restaurant's own preparation reference. If it does not answer the guest's question, verify with the kitchen.

q: Which set contains only preparations listed on the ramen wall chart?
choices: Miso Ramen, Chicken Shio Ramen, Curry Ramen
Dragon Ramen, Miso Ramen, Chicken Shio Ramen
Tonkotsu Ramen, Pad Thai, Curry Ramen
Tokyo Shoyu Ramen, Volcano Udon, Tantanmen Ramen
why: Miso, Chicken Shio, and Curry Ramen are all listed. The other options include items not shown on this reference.

q: A guest asks whether a dish is safe for a serious sesame allergy. You are not certain what is in the sauce. What should you do?
choices: Say it should be fine if sesame is not visible
Recommend the dish marked Vegan
Check the restaurant's allergen reference and verify with the kitchen under procedure
Suggest they remove the garnish
why: Never infer allergen safety from appearance, a dish name, or a dietary label. Verify ingredients and handling with the kitchen and follow restaurant procedures.

q: Which of these appears as an allergen category on the ramen wall chart?
choices: Shellfish
Coconut
Mustard
Celery
why: Shellfish is one of the chart's printed allergen categories. The chart also lists Egg, Wheat, Dairy, Soy, Sesame, Seafood, and Nuts.

q: What three kinds of information are organized on the ramen wall chart?
choices: Preparation, toppings, and allergens
Prices, calories, and spice ratings
Cooking times, staff names, and table numbers
Guest reviews, portion sizes, and discounts
why: The chart is a practical reference for how the ramen is prepared, its toppings, and its listed allergen markings.

q: A guest asks whether Vegan Ramen is automatically safe for their wheat allergy. What is the accurate response?
choices: Yes, vegan means allergen-free
Yes, because wheat is not an animal product
Do not assume; check the documented ingredients and verify with the kitchen
Tell them to order it without toppings
why: Vegan does not mean wheat-free or free from cross-contact. Check the relevant allergen information and kitchen procedures before answering.

q: A guest asks you to compare Miso Ramen and Tokyo Shoyu Ramen, but you cannot recall the approved flavor descriptions. What should you do?
choices: Invent a confident-sounding comparison
Use the approved menu reference or ask the kitchen, then explain the verified difference
Tell them all ramen tastes basically the same
Recommend whichever costs more
why: A useful comparison must be accurate. Do not improvise ingredients or flavor claims when you are unsure.

q: Which preparation is listed on the chart alongside the ramen dishes, even though its name is not a ramen variety?
choices: Stir Fried Noodles
Pad Thai
Tempura Udon
Poke Bowl
why: Stir Fried Noodles is included as one of the eight preparations on the employee reference.

q: What is the strongest foundation for recommending a menu item to a guest?
choices: Choose the item with the highest price
Repeat the same recommendation to every table
Understand what the guest enjoys and match it to a menu item you can describe accurately
Recommend something even after the guest declines
why: Good recommendations are relevant, informed, and guest-centered. Respect a decline and never invent details.
